reach: PRODUCTION. The one SUPPORTED report either MCP tool can return rests on exactly this level: thermal_models.lumped's `analytic_reference_agreement`. The hard benchmark scores MCP verdicts, so this rule is scored there and the benchmark is re-run.
what_was_already_seen: the audited reproduction only: `ValidationCheck(PASS, establishes=ANALYTICALLY_VERIFIED, evidence=('trust me',))` is constructed, attained, survives from_dict and carries a SUPPORTED verdict, while the same construction claiming BENCHMARK_VALIDATED or CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED is refused -- and that the production lumped check carries a prose evidence string and a tolerance the domain computes per solve, with no threshold record and no oracle record

the three analytic references in src/ and their expressions, read to write the registry: thermal_models.lumped.series_recurrence, thermal.conduction1d.single_mode_analytic, kinetics.cstr.adiabatic_reaction_free_invariant, and that conduction1d and cstr already write a DECLARED threshold record into their checks' evidence while lumped writes none
NOTHING about how any rule below scores on the hard benchmark or anywhere else

analytically_verified_needs_a_pinned_ref.rule: A check that PASSes or WARNs and declares ANALYTICALLY_VERIFIED must carry, in its evidence, exactly one `analytic-reference:<id>` line, exactly one `analytic-reference-digest:sha256:<hex>` line, the literal line `analytic-authority:repository-pinned`, and exactly one `thresholds:<gate>@<version>#<fingerprint>` record. The reference id must be registered in a new `SCIENTIFIC_ANALYTIC_REFERENCE_DECLARATIONS` table on `engcore.domains`; the digest must equal the registered digest of the reference's own expression; and the threshold record must name the gate that registration says awards this reference's level, with a set that `is_declared`.
analytically_verified_needs_a_pinned_ref.why_this_shape: it is the oracle rule's shape, which the audit names as the model: identity, content digest, a pinned authority line, and a re-verification against a registry the caller does not hold. The threshold record is the consensus rule's second half: the level belongs to the domain that awards it, and a set that is not the domain's own awards nothing. Neither is invented here.
analytically_verified_needs_a_pinned_ref.what_it_refuses: a hand-written check, however worded. `evidence=('trust me',)` carries no reference line; a fabricated `analytic-reference:` line names an unregistered id; a copied line whose digest does not match the registered expression is refused; and a `thresholds:` record the caller built is not is_declared.
analytically_verified_needs_a_pinned_ref.what_it_does_not_refuse: a check copied verbatim from a genuine solve onto another result. That residual is the core's own, stated in `_issuer_gap`, and is unchanged: closing it needs the record bound to the result it qualifies, which the frozen check shape has no field for.
analytically_verified_needs_a_pinned_ref.class: A (a re-verification against a pinned registry; no threshold)
analytically_verified_needs_a_pinned_ref.measured_outcome: implemented, with the record it reads CHANGED from the preregistered one -- see amendment_log entry 1. The hand-written check, an unregistered reference, a changed closed form, two references, a missing or doubled threshold record, another domain's declared set and a caller-built set are all refused. Both production producers keep the level. The hard benchmark re-scored identically.

the_registry_pins_the_statement_and_not_.rule: The registry pins each reference's id, version, the module constant that declares it, the reference EXPRESSION as a string, and the SHA-256 of that expression. It does not pin the implementing module's source bytes.
the_registry_pins_the_statement_and_not_.why: what makes the level meaningful is WHICH closed form the solve was compared against, and that is the expression. A source digest would move on every edit to a file, including edits that do not touch the formula, and would make the level brittle rather than bound. The three expressions are: thermal_models.lumped.series_recurrence -> sha256 2534eb18c91ca70e9dbd156ce76b824a75c2f595f3cb05f16eaab77352fd5ba4; thermal.conduction1d.single_mode_analytic -> a8564c9933fbad5abed6e16fd6f12188a3318872b27b8489f0222a04aee5f1c6; kinetics.cstr.adiabatic_reaction_free_invariant -> 0fb7efc02108e3d14f7b0369ea83ddbdfebcbc7834b153c11bee14161681693b. Each is recomputed at import from the constant it names, so the table and the constant cannot drift apart silently -- the same discipline the threshold table already uses.
the_registry_pins_the_statement_and_not_.measured_outcome: implemented as stated. The registry pins the expression and its digest; the digest is the drift guard between the table and the constant, asserted by tests/test_core_scientific_audit_batch9.py::test_r04_the_registry_and_the_constants_it_names_cannot_drift, and is NOT a line the check carries -- see amendment_log entry 1.

the_lumped_reference_gate_is_declared.rule: thermal_models.lumped gains a declared VerificationThresholds set, `thermal_models.lumped.analytic_reference` at version 0.1.0, holding the rounding budget its tolerance is built from (`rounding_ulps`), registered in SCIENTIFIC_THRESHOLD_DECLARATIONS. Its analytic check awards through `thresholds.award` and writes `thresholds.evidence()`.
the_lumped_reference_gate_is_declared.why_a_gate_at_all: the level belongs to the domain that awards it, and until now the lumped check's tolerance was a number the module computed with nothing declared behind it. The value that IS a policy choice is the rounding budget; the rest of the tolerance is the reference's own reported error bound, which is a measurement and not a threshold.
the_lumped_reference_gate_is_declared.the_number: SOLVER_ROUNDING_ULPS, unchanged, moved from a module constant into the declared set's `rounding_ulps`. No number changes value in this batch.
the_lumped_reference_gate_is_declared.class: A (an existing number, given an owner)

the_tolerance_is_not_re_derived.rule: The issuer rule does NOT re-derive the check's tolerance from the declared set, as the consensus rule does. It requires a declared set to be named and nothing more about the tolerance's value.
the_tolerance_is_not_re_derived.why_not: the lumped tolerance is the reference's own per-solve error bound plus a rounding budget, and the conduction and cstr tolerances are relative errors down a refinement ladder. None is a single declared number the check's tolerance must equal, so the consensus rule's equality test does not apply and asserting one would be inventing a criterion these gates do not read. Recorded as a residual rather than approximated.

compatibility_impact.the_verdict_word: UNCHANGED as a vocabulary. Whether any PARTICULAR verdict moves is a measurement, not a choice, and the hard benchmark is re-scored to find out. The intent is that it does not: the three production producers are given real issuer records, so the levels they award stay earned. If a production verdict does move, that is reported and not hidden.

amendment_log.what: the record the rule reads is the line the producers ALREADY wrote, and there is no new evidence line, no carried digest and no authority line
amendment_log.preregistered: the check's evidence must carry exactly one `analytic-reference:<id>` line, one `analytic-reference-digest:sha256:<hex>` line, the literal `analytic-authority:repository-pinned`, and one `thresholds:` record.
amendment_log.implemented: the check's evidence must name exactly one REGISTERED reference as `"<id>: <expression>"`, with the expression equal to the registered one byte for byte, and carry exactly one `thresholds:` record equal to the awarding gate's declared identity and fingerprint.
amendment_log.why_1_the_pin: src/engcore/domains/thermal/ is SHA-256 pinned by the frozen thermal_t1, t2 and t3 experiments, whose central claim is that their measured bias is a property of THAT solver. Adding an evidence line to thermal/conduction1d/validation.py broke the pin (tests/test_thermal_t1_fidelity_inference.py::test_frozen_thermal_solver_digests_match caught it immediately). That pin is evidence this work has no authority to spend, exactly as engcore/domains/__init__.py already says for the same tree, so the rule is written to the records the producers already keep.
amendment_log.why_2_the_stronger_reason: a digest of a PUBLIC value carries no more authority than the value. The oracle rule needs one because an oracle's evidence is data the caller does not hold; an analytic reference's expression is in the source. Comparing the expression in full is the same strength as comparing a digest of it, with one step fewer. So the two carried lines the preregistration asked for were ceremony, and the authority is where it always was: the registry (this id is one the repository stands behind) and the declared threshold set (which a caller cannot forge).
amendment_log.what_this_costs: the rule has exactly the strength of the ORACLE rule the audit named as the model, and no more: every line it requires is reproducible from public data, so it refuses a careless or invented claim and not a determined forgery. The core already states that residual in _issuer_gap ('what this cannot do is tell an issued record from a faithful copy of one'), and it is unchanged. The CONSENSUS rule is stronger, because its binding lines carry a digest over the run's own numbers -- data a caller does not have unless they ran it. An analytic reference has no equivalent.

amendment_log.what: the three-part threshold comparison became one, because the batch-9 mutation run showed two parts were dead code
amendment_log.detail: the first implementation checked the gate name, the version and the values fingerprint separately. Two mutations SURVIVED: all three compared against the gate the REGISTRY names rather than the one the record names, so each was subsumed by the fingerprint comparison. The implementation now makes one comparison of the whole `<gate>@<version>#<fingerprint>` line against the registry's, and B9d/B9e mutate that one line against the two cases it covers. A survivor that buys the removal of dead code from a guard is a survivor doing its job.
amendment_log.effect_on_the_rules_already_scored: none; the rule is the same rule, expressed once.

amendment_log.what: B9h is recorded as an EXPECTED SURVIVOR, and what that admits
amendment_log.detail: mutating the lumped check to award ANALYTICALLY_VERIFIED beside its gate rather than through `thresholds.award(...)` leaves the level in place, because the check still writes a valid threshold record and the issuer gap is what enforces it. LUMPED_ANALYTIC_REFERENCE_THRESHOLDS is a module constant and LumpedThermalSolver takes no `thresholds=` argument, so there is no caller override for `award` to withhold from. `award` is kept -- it is the one place a future `thresholds=` argument would be judged, and every other gate in the repository reads this way -- but it is NOT load-bearing in lumped today, and the mutation log and the audit document say so rather than counting it as a killed guard.
amendment_log.the_change_that_would_make_it_load_beari: give LumpedThermalSolver a keyword-only `thresholds: VerificationThresholds = LUMPED_ANALYTIC_REFERENCE_THRESHOLDS` and thread it to _reference_check, which is what the other three gates do. Additive, and out of I-09's scope; recorded as a residual.
